the atherosclerosing process in femoral arteries is an age-related disease and that the inflammatory component of atherosclerosis is more prominent than the calcification component in this disease.
atherosclerosis in the femoral artery increases with age, and this progression is mainly due to the progression of the inflammatory process.
the 18F-FGD PET scan reflects the atherosclerosis activity, and the MDP bone scan reflects the atheroma severity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inflammatory component of atherosclerosis progresses faster with age, while the severity of calcification progresses slower.
the inflammatory component of atherosclerosis progresses more rapidly with age, while the calcification component progresses with a slower pace.
the 18F-FGD uptake ratio is a more sensitive and reliable indicator than the MDP ratio for the evaluation of atherosclerosis in the femoral region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uptake ratios of MDP/BKG and 18F-BKG in femoral arteries are the best indicators of atherosclerosis and its severity.
18F-FGD and MDP PET scans may be used to assess the progression of the inflammatory and calcification components of the atherosclerosis process in femoral arteries.
atherosclerostic activity in the femoral artery is not a static phenomenon, and it progresses with age.
